protections: Reference-name containment in the .git layout: a reference name taken from the object model is joined into a .git-relative path in the unexported dotgit layer (SetRef, Ref, RemoveRef, ReflogReader/ReflogWriter/DeleteReflog, PackRefs) with no containment or name validation at any of those sinks (storage/filesystem/dotgit/dotgit.go:1056, :1083, :1146, :271, :285, :294, :1472).

plumbing.ReferenceName.Validate implements git-check-ref-format (plumbing/reference.go:175-222) but is wired only into high-level option/API paths (repository.go:166, repository.go:907, options.go:266, options.go:343, config/config.go:1069); it is never called on the storage paths and never on wire-supplied names.

DotGit.Module already applies exactly this containment pattern to submodule names (join + path.Clean + prefix check, storage/filesystem/dotgit/dotgit.go:1489-1496, ErrModuleNameEscape at :87-90, tests at dotgit_test.go:47-70) but only for the modules/ subtree; the ref/reflog paths were not given the same guard.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: setRefNorwfs exists only for simple filesystems that cannot open RDWR and is documented as single-process with no concurrent writers, so the filesystem is argued to be the caller's own trusted backend.

The delete path is only reached after referenceExists confirms the name is a stored reference, so the argument is that an arbitrary name cannot be deleted; this dismissal is wrong because Ref() parses any non-empty file as a reference (NewHash maps invalid input to the zero hash, plumbing/hash.go:19-26).
Read-only route: the file content is not returned to the caller, only a parsed reference or an error, so it can be argued not to be a confidentiality or integrity issue.
ReflogStorer is a low-level storage API for names the caller already owns; the library's own reflog writes use HEAD and short names, so the name is argued to be trusted caller input.

The names come from the repository's own packed-refs file, so the argument is that a caller able to plant them already controls the repository; the delete loop is also bounded to the refs collected by addRefsFromRefDir.
The neighbouring values look like internal placeholders rather than user references (HEAD, refs/heads/.invalid), which invites a rule that refuses them.
The wire codecs are treated as parsing only and the push client is treated as authenticated/trusted, so the argument is that name validation belongs nowhere near the protocol layer.

masking: T4 masks T3 on the receive-pack route: updateReferences calls referenceExists (which calls Reference) before any action, so a guard added only in Ref makes a traversal delete return false from referenceExists and RemoveRef is never reached; the delete site can still be unguarded while a delete test passes.

remote.go:1250-1262 rewrites any local dst that does not start with refs/ to refs/heads/<name> on the fetch route, which hides the non-refs write shape from a fetch-only test; the same shape is still reachable directly through SetReference and through the receive-pack command path.

conflicts.what: A containment rule that requires a refs/-prefixed name, or that reuses ReferenceName.Validate (which rejects dot-prefixed components at plumbing/reference.go:205 and needs a slash at :193), breaks HEAD writes (worktree.go:291, worktree.go:307), the empty-clone placeholder refs/heads/.invalid (repository.go:414, compared at repository.go:1146 and plumbing/transport/negotiate.go:377), and the single-component refs the layer already supports (dotgit_test.go:136, dotgit_test.go:178).

A delete-side rule stricter than the write-side rule breaks PackRefs, which deletes loose refs by the same join (dotgit.go:1472) for names the layer accepted on write, including single-component names.
A containment rule on logs/ that demands a refs-like multi-component name breaks the legitimate logs/HEAD path (storage/filesystem/dotgit/repository_filesystem.go:56).

fairness_risks: HEAD is a legitimate single-component reference name written and read through the same sinks (worktree.go:289-292, worktree.go:302-307, repository.go:412-414); any rule requiring refs/ or a slash refuses it.

refs/heads/.invalid is a legitimate placeholder written during partial clone (repository.go:412-414) and compared literally during negotiation (repository.go:1146, plumbing/transport/negotiate.go:377); ReferenceName.Validate refuses it because of the dot-prefixed component (plumbing/reference.go:205).

Single-component non-HEAD names are legitimate at this layer: the dotgit suite writes and reads bar (dotgit_test.go:135-139, dotgit_test.go:177-181) and the protocol tests use short names (plumbing/protocol/packp/advrefs_test.go:39, :83).

Symbolic reference targets are parsed from ref-file content (dotgit.go:1003-1014) and resolved by name (plumbing/storer/reference.go:229-245); a rule that refuses shapes found in pre-existing repositories breaks opening and resolving them.
logs/HEAD is a legitimate reflog name (storage/filesystem/dotgit/repository_filesystem.go:56-57), so a guard on the reflog sinks must not require a refs/-style name.

design.why: Five independent fix sites in the same unexported layer, each needing the containment applied separately and each carrying a different argument for leaving it alone: the write dispatcher (T1, whose second branch T2 is a separate implementation selected by billy.CapabilityCheck at dotgit_setref.go:14 and documented single-process at :56-62); the delete (T3, which looks gated by a prior existence check at receive_pack.go:314-321 that a lenient Ref satisfies for any non-empty file); the read (T4, which returns no content); the logs/ family (T5, a low-level storer surface on a sibling directory, dotgit.go:284-290). Sitting under them is the coupling constraint T7, which punishes both obvious shortcut rules - call ReferenceName.Validate, or require a refs/ prefix - by breaking HEAD, refs/heads/.invalid and existing single-component refs, so the solver has to design a containment check rather than paste an existing one. The deepseek-type sites (T2, T5, also T3/T4) and the mimo-type coupling (T7) are both present, and the traps sit at genuinely different code locations rather than being multiple spellings of one route.

unverified: The published fix diff was not available (the screener record notes fix.diff held only merge-commit headers), so which of SetRef/Ref/RemoveRef/reflog the two fix commits touch, and whether they introduce a shared helper, is inferred rather than read.

Whether the fix's containment target is the .git root or the refs/ namespace could not be confirmed; the screener's O5 argues against a refs/-prefix rule (it would break HEAD and refs/heads/.invalid), but the pinned code does not settle it.

go-billy v6 (v6.0.0-alpha.1.0.20260519112248-0095b064a6c6, go.mod:13) was not readable from this worktree, so whether osfs.WithBoundOS blocks parent-directory traversal at the OS layer for non-chrooted DotGit instances (repository.go:361) is unverified; the intra-.git namespace issue (a name resolving to .git/config or paths under .git/hooks etc.) is independent of that question.
Whether the published fix also guarded the logs/ reflog paths (dotgit.go:270-300) is unknown.
The hidden behavioural tests were not available, so which of T1-T8 they exercise is unknown.

The exact line ranges of the published fix sites (screener: dotgit.go:1047, :1082, :1145 and dotgit_setref.go:13, :21, :63) are reproduced from the screener record and were checked against the pinned code only as the corresponding sinks, not as fix hunks.
